guide.title: New Milford, Connecticut: Roger Sherman's Town Green
guide.intro: New Milford was settled in 1707 by John Noble, Sr., of Westfield, Massachusetts, and his eight-year-old daughter Sarah, and the town incorporated in 1712. Its most famous resident, Roger Sherman, lived here before moving to New Haven in 1761 and went on to sign both the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution; the lot of his former house is the site of today's Town Hall. New Milford is Connecticut's largest town by total area, at 63.7 square miles. Tobacco cultivation and warehouses drove its economy by the late 1800s, alongside factories producing buttons, paint and varnish, hats, and furnishings. During the Revolutionary War the town sent 285 men to fight out of a population of 2,776, and the 7th Connecticut Regiment was raised here on September 16, 1776.

sections.heading: Roger Sherman's town
sections.body: Roger Sherman is the reason New Milford shows up in national history — before he moved to New Haven in 1761, he lived on the lot that is now the town's Town Hall, and he went on to sign both the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution. The town's own Revolutionary War contribution was substantial for its size: 285 men out of a population of 2,776, with the 7th Connecticut Regiment raised in town on September 16, 1776. By the late 1800s, tobacco warehouses and factories making buttons, paint and varnish, hats, and furnishings had replaced agriculture as the main economy.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: New Milford is a drive-to destination: exit I-84 at Danbury and drive roughly 12-14 miles north on US Route 7 or US Route 202 — the two highways intersect and merge to form the town's main corridor — with CT Route 67 also serving the town. New Milford is about 80 miles from Midtown Manhattan. There's no passenger rail station in town; the closest is Metro-North's Danbury Branch terminus in Danbury, about 14 miles south. Tracks running north through New Milford now carry Housatonic Railroad freight only, and a long-studied extension of passenger service to New Milford has never been built.

sections.heading: The green, a flea market, and Main Street
sections.body: New Milford's long town green anchors the center, with Lovers Leap State Park and its 1895 Berlin Iron Bridge over the Housatonic gorge. The Elephant's Trunk Country Flea Market, the largest weekly flea market in New England, marked its 50th anniversary in 2026 with its usual Sunday season, April through December. TheatreWorks New Milford and the Bank Street Theater cover live theater and independent film downtown, and Housatonic River Brewing and Contempo Kitchen & Bar are among the newer names on the dining scene, alongside the historic Homestead Inn.

faq.question: How do I get to New Milford?
faq.answer: By car: exit I-84 at Danbury and drive roughly 12-14 miles north on US Route 7 or US Route 202. There's no passenger rail station in town; the nearest is Metro-North's Danbury Branch terminus in Danbury, about 14 miles south.

faq.question: Who was Roger Sherman?
faq.answer: New Milford's most famous resident before he moved to New Haven in 1761. Sherman signed both the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution; the lot of his former New Milford house is the site of today's Town Hall.

faq.question: Is New Milford really Connecticut's largest town?
faq.answer: By total area, yes — 63.7 square miles (61.6 of it land, 2.2 water), ahead of second-place Greenwich at 47.62 square miles.

faq.question: What is the Elephant's Trunk Flea Market?
faq.answer: Billed as the largest weekly flea market in New England, operating since 1976 and marking its 50th anniversary in 2026. It runs every Sunday, April through December, with $4 general admission.

faq.question: Where can I eat and stay in New Milford?
faq.answer: Housatonic River Brewing and Contempo Kitchen & Bar are two of downtown's newer dining spots. The Homestead Inn, on the north end of the Village Green, has welcomed guests since 1928.

places.name: New Milford Historical Society & Museum
places.summary: Exhibits artifacts and photographs of the town from Indigenous peoples to modern times, including the colonial-era Knapp House and a colonial garden. Admission $5 adults, children under 12 free. Open Tuesday-Saturday 11 a.m.-2 p.m., and by appointment.

places.name: Lovers Leap State Park
places.address: 178 Still River Drive, New Milford, CT 06776
places.summary: A 160-acre park over the Housatonic River gorge featuring an 1895 Berlin Iron Bridge — one of only four remaining lenticular truss bridges in Connecticut — and the Lovers Leap rock overlook. Four miles of trails, free admission, open daily 8 a.m. to sunset.

photos.title: Housatonic River at Lovers Leap
photos.description: The Housatonic River gorge in autumn color, seen from the Lovers Leap bridge.
photos.author: Bob P. B.

places.name: Harrybrooke Park & Harden House Museum
places.address: 100 Still River Drive, New Milford, CT 06776
places.summary: A nonprofit park open 365 days a year with walking and cycling paths and picnic pavilions, on the grounds of a former weekend estate. The on-site Harden House Museum is not on a published tour schedule — call 860-799-6520 to arrange a visit.

places.name: TheatreWorks New Milford
places.address: 5 Brookside Avenue (parking GPS: 20 Elm Street Extension), New Milford, CT 06776
places.summary: Community theater founded in 1967 as the New Milford Players and renamed TheatreWorks in 1992; stages a year-round season of plays and musicals.

places.name: Bank Street Theater
places.summary: Downtown New Milford's independent movie house on historic Bank Street, showing first-run and specialty films. Check the site's ticketing system for current showtimes.

places.name: Elephant's Trunk Country Flea Market
places.summary: Billed as the largest weekly flea market in New England, operating since 1976 and celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026. Runs every Sunday, April through December, general admission $4, gates open 7 a.m.-2 p.m.

places.name: Housatonic River Brewing
places.summary: Craft brewery with a full kitchen and live music, taproom hours Wednesday-Thursday 4-9 p.m., Friday 3-10 p.m., Saturday 1-10 p.m., Sunday 1-7 p.m.

places.name: Contempo Kitchen & Bar
places.summary: Mediterranean restaurant, a 'Popular' listing in the Greater New Milford Chamber of Commerce directory. Open Tuesday-Saturday 11:30 a.m.-10 p.m., Sunday 11:30 a.m.-9 p.m.; closed Monday.

places.name: The Homestead Inn
places.summary: Historic inn on the north end of New Milford's Village Green, welcoming guests since 1928, with 16 rooms across the Main House and the 1938-built Treadwell Annex.
